newsitem.title: USA: Outflows from US junk bond mutual funds accelerate.
newsitem.headline: Outflows from US junk bond mutual funds accelerate.

text.p: Investors pulled a net $422.8 million in cash out of U.S. high-yield mutual funds in the week ended March 26 as the exodus from the junk bond market accelerated, Robert Adler, president of AMG Data Services, said Friday.
"We've seen outflows of three-quarters of a billion dollars, or about one percent of total high-yield mutual fund assets, over the past two weeks," said Adler.
Weekly cash flows into high-yield mutual funds turned negative two weeks ago for the first time since October 16, 1996.

Analysts said the outflows followed weakness in the Treasury market during the month of March, as well as recent comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan suggesting that junk bonds may be overvalued.
Adler said that while the outflows were relatively large compared to past activity, it was premature to identify a trend.

"I think we need to wait to see if this is just in response to recent bond market activity and comments by the (Fed) chairman, or is representative of a longer-term trend of negative investor sentiment," he said.

Adler said that among 239 high-yield funds tracked by AMG, representing around $84 billion in assets, about half experienced net outflows in the latest week, roughly the same number as in the prior week.

The funds with the largest net outflows were Zurich Kemper Investment's High-Yield A with $89 million, Strong Capital Management's high-yield with $65 million, and Pimco Advisors LP's high-yield with $45 million, he said.
Fifteen funds had net outflows of $10 million or more, he said.
AMG, based in Arcata, Calif., is a U.S. mutual fund information company.
